job: Make the strongest fact this project owns visible: the same home, line by line, owner-orchestrated against builder-delivered — and what the difference actually costs you.
priority: Highest of the open set. A judge gives this sixty seconds, and this is the only thing on the site that lands in ten.
origin: Founder direction, 2026-08-14: prioritise the most dramatic and useful change. Proposed by an external review as a GSAP/Lenis scroll piece; the visualisation is adopted, the two new animation dependencies are not — see rejectionGates.
context: THE NUMBERS ARE ALREADY ANCHORED AND ALREADY PROVEN. data/alberta/cost-model.json holds `totalsExLand` — $199,100 / $301,280 / $443,900 LOW/MID/HIGH for the 800 sqft off-grid SIP reference build — and `agent/ npm run demo` reconciles them to the dollar as a release gate. Do not recompute them, do not round them, do not retype them. Read them.

THE COMPARISON IS ALSO ALREADY SOURCED, at cost-model.json:27: `builderComparison: { low: 450000, high: 650000, basis: "Same home builder-delivered ex-land at $250-450/sqft hard + 25-40% soft; owner-builder saves 30-40% ($150-250K) for 12-24 months of labour" }`. Use that object. The basis string is not decoration — it is what makes the comparison sayable.

THE BRAND GUIDE HAS ALREADY RULED ON THE WORDING, twice. BRAND-VOICE-GUIDE.md:250 bans 'Up to 40% coordination margins' as unsourced and prescribes the defensible sentence: 'a conventional builder delivers this reference home at $450-650K'. It is a RANGE, not '$450,000+'. Match that.

THE HONEST VERSION IS THE BETTER ONE. The saving is 30-40% IN EXCHANGE FOR 12-24 MONTHS OF THE OWNER'S LABOUR. A margin story that shows the money and hides the labour is the exact hype this brand exists to refuse — and it is also less persuasive, because everyone reading knows the money came from somewhere. The trade IS the story.

WHAT EXISTS TO BUILD ON: lib/builder/projectBudget.ts (createProjectBudget, with confidence, gaps and a cap comparison), the /budget route and its .budget-* CSS system, the LiveReadout strip in the builder, and a motion system with named 150-250ms tokens plus a damped house curve. components/design/ecoSpec.ts has the money formatters.
SCROLL CHOREOGRAPHY ALREADY EXISTS in the story scene and is pinned by the landing specs — read how it is done there before inventing a second mechanism.
doNotTouch: data/alberta/cost-model.json — this node READS the anchor. Changing it breaks the money gate.

app/lib/builder/projectBudget.ts — if you need a number it does not expose, report that rather than adding a second calculation. A parallel cost path is the divergence class that has bitten this repo three times.
app/components/builder/BuilderApp.tsx — VW03 owns it this wave.
README.md, docs/SUBMISSION.md, app/package.json, app/playwright.ui.config.ts, app/tests/gate-coverage.spec.ts — orchestrator-owned.
rejectionGates: NO NEW ANIMATION DEPENDENCY. The review that proposed this asked for GSAP and Lenis in the same breath as asking to strip 77 KB of wallet code off every route — those two asks contradict each other and the byte-stripping one wins. `motion` is already here, the motion tokens are already here, and prefers-reduced-motion is already honoured at the token level. Use them. If you genuinely cannot express the piece without a library, STOP and report rather than installing one.

EVERY FIGURE TRACES TO cost-model.json. Not one hardcoded dollar amount in the component. Assert it: the spec should read the JSON and assert the rendered figures match, so a drifted number goes red rather than shipping a confident wrong total on the page people make money decisions from.

THE LABOUR COST IS NOT OPTIONAL AND MUST BE VISIBLE IN THE SAME VIEW AS THE SAVING — not in a footnote, not behind a disclosure, not further down. 12-24 months of the owner's labour, stated plainly, at the moment the saving is shown. Assert its presence in the spec. A future 'tightening' that drops it must fail the build.
THE COMPARISON IS A RANGE WITH A BASIS. $450,000-$650,000, with the basis sentence reachable. Never '$450,000+', never a single number, never an unsourced percentage.
IT IS AN ESTIMATE AND SAYS SO. The standing label rule: `estimate, not a quote` travels with the noun. This is the surface where that matters most.
prefers-reduced-motion must reach the same information. Someone who cannot take the animation still gets the whole comparison — assert the content is present with motion reduced.
CLS <= 0.08 is a pinned gate. Reserve space; do not animate layout.
instructions: 1. Read cost-model.json's totalsExLand and builderComparison, projectBudget.ts, and the /budget page, before designing anything.

2. Build the margin stack: the line items that make up the owner-orchestrated total, accumulating against the builder-delivered range, so the delta assembles itself out of real lines rather than being asserted. The reference build is 800 sqft off-grid SIP — say which build it is, because a comparison of unlike things is worthless.

3. Motion serves comprehension, not spectacle. Each line should be readable as it lands. If the animation makes the numbers harder to read, it is wrong — and static must be a first-class rendering, not a degraded one.
4. Say what the owner actually does for the money: the 12-24 months, the coordination, the fact that this platform is an orchestrator and never the general contractor.

5. Spec: figures match the JSON; the labour trade is present; the comparison renders as a range with its basis; the estimate label is present; reduced motion still delivers the full content; no hardcoded dollar amounts in the component source.

verify.note: the money anchor is the hard gate — the demo must still reconcile to the dollar

evidence.note: The /budget cost-margin story shipped in 4e72f72; money anchor still $199,100 / $301,280 / $443,900.
